- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% deviation), check sentiment for bullish momentum — if sentiment is fading, reduce forecast to reflect mean reversion.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., >10% deviation), sentiment is often bearish — increase forecast by 2–5% to capture sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to be 1–2% higher than true outcome for the first 3–5 days of the horizon.
- When sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– values), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying correction.
